goal: Play as a brand-new player who has never heard of the game, following the HUD's NEXT line (top left) from the first afternoon until you have slept at home and woken the next morning; then try V. Note every moment of confusion, and answer the questions at the end.

findings.title: Lamp-lit wall washes out the HUD at the door
findings.detail: At my door with the lamp lit the white HUD text sits on a pale yellow wall and is barely readable. Seen in earlier runs.
findings.repro: after the third rope, walk to the indigo door with the lamp lit

findings.title: Walking into a house wall with the view pitched up looks like an invisible block
findings.detail: With the view tilted up (sky in the top half), a house wall filled the lower half as flat black and W did nothing for several seconds; only S and a turn showed it was a wall. Not a collision bug, but nothing on screen says you are against a wall.
findings.repro: on the way to the ghat, look up and walk into a house side

findings.title: The opening hint overlaps the help block
findings.detail: At the start the orange hint lines are drawn over the white help text. Known from earlier runs.

verdict: Followed NEXT from the first afternoon to the morning of 22 March and then V, with no blocker. The dream showed 'Nothing to do; the dream passes by itself' and the deep sleep 'Deep sleep. Morning comes by itself.', so the sleep never read as a hang (#37 fixed). Remaining friction is HUD legibility at 640x360. secondsToObjective are wall-clock seconds from pt start (no probe); this session was driven by the proctor, interleaved with another session, on a shared machine, so the times are long. The proctor had read the #39 diff, so this is not a naive first-time read.

answers.question: In your own words, what did you think the game was about? What did the rope and the snake, and the clay and the pots, mean?
answers.answer: The named pots are one clay: the names and shapes are real as uses but the stuff is one, and breaking a pot loses nothing of the clay. The snake on the path was a rope all along; fear came from not seeing in poor light and ended when I held the lamp and looked steadily. Sleep extends it: waking, dream and deep sleep came and went, and the waking text says you were there for all three.

answers.question: Did anything feel preachy, confusing, or inaccurate (in the teaching, the verses in the codex, or how the tradition is described)? Say what and where; if nothing did, say so.
answers.answer: Nothing felt preachy: the game shows, and the codex quotes its sources with Sanskrit and a named translation. 'Other schools' gives Visistadvaita and Dvaita fair, short readings and says the game follows one school. The sleep no longer confused me. I cannot judge the translations, some of which are marked as working translations awaiting review.
